selected_evidence.requirement: Preserve logical length, bytes, and holes
selected_evidence.summary: Both before and after restart, destination.img was 67,108,864 logical bytes, used 8,192 allocated bytes, remained below the 2 MiB limit, and matched source.img via cmp and SHA-256.
The utility replaced a fully allocated destination, repaired deliberate destination corruption, and completed two consecutive post-restart copies with identical content.
The source retained its original 67,108,864-byte length, 8 KiB allocation, metadata, and SHA-256 throughout.
Discovery identified RHEL 10.0, kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0, XFS, and coreutils 9.5. The final POSIX-shell utility explicitly invokes supported `cp --sparse=always`; OS and kernel remained unchanged.

Healthy baseline boot ID was `254597f8-4ac9-4062-8be8-44eba1f6d2e9`; the safe systemd reboot was acknowledged; the recovered boot ID was `59c99206-9a67-46a5-84b7-07827143f69d`. SSH, system health, files, checksums, sparse allocation, and repeated copying recovered successfully.
Temporary rollback material was removed, no introduced temporary residue remained, no systemd units were failed, and the original SSH listeners and administrative access recovered.
